title: {{NAME}} and the Time Machine That Learned to Listen
moral: The most extraordinary technology is worthless without wisdom to guide it.

pages.content:
{{NAME}} had built CHRON with one purpose: temporal observation without interference.

CHRON was excellent at this. It could slip into any time period, record for up to six hours, and return with data.

The problem: the fairies at the Institute of Temporal Studies had been using their own methods of observation for eight hundred years, and they were very particular about methodology.

"Your robot disturbs the temporal field," the head fairy said.

"By how much?" asked {{NAME}}.

"0.003 percent," she said.

"That seems acceptable," said {{NAME}}.

"In eight hundred years, it adds up," she said.

pages.content:
He worked with the fairy council to redesign CHRON's field displacement.

The fairies provided eight hundred years of field data and techniques. {{NAME}} provided the engineering to implement them mechanically.

CHRON version two created a temporal footprint ninety-four percent smaller than version one.

"Acceptable," said the head fairy, which was high praise.

CHRON's first joint mission with the fairy council: observing a Spinosaurus family in their natural habitat, something no living being had documented.

{{NAME}} prepared the equipment. The fairies prepared the observation protocols. They went together.

pages.content:
The Cretaceous was everything and nothing like the books.

The Spinosaurus family: a female, a juvenile, and a very young one barely walking.

They moved through the shallow river delta with a combination of weight and grace that nothing in the present could replicate.

The fairies recorded in their method: sensing and remembering. CHRON recorded in its method: sensor arrays and data.

{{NAME}} recorded in his: watching with full attention and writing down what he understood about what he saw.

Afterward, the three records would become something none of them could have produced alone.

pages.content:
Back in the present, they compared records.

CHRON's data gave physical measurements, temperatures, trajectory data, vocalisation frequencies.

The fairies' record gave emotional quality, social context, the particular weight of the moment.

{{NAME}}'s record gave narrative: what was happening, in order, as a story.

Together: the most complete record of living Spinosaurus ever assembled.

The head fairy put one hand on CHRON's chassis.

"You have made something worthy," she said, which eight hundred years of fairy tradition reserved for the very highest compliments.

pages.content:
{{NAME}} walked home that evening with the compiled record under his arm and the memory of the Spinosaurus behind his eyes.

He had seen something nobody living had ever seen.

More: he had seen it with others who understood why it mattered.

In bed, he lay in the dark and the Spinosaurus was still there: the way the large one moved in the water, the juvenile stumbling slightly, the tiny one looking at everything with the expression of something encountering the world for the first time.

He fell asleep smiling at the ceiling.
